overview: The Medford Traffic Commission met to consider several parking permit variances, crosswalk daylighting, and a proposal for on-street electric vehicle charging stations. The Commission denied a parking variance on Winthrop Street but approved related traffic safety and neighborhood connectivity measures, approved a parking variance on Henry Street, and received public feedback on the proposed charging station locations.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the previous meeting.

items.title: 2025-60: Handicap Placard Sign at 71 Central Avenue
items.summary: Tabled the application because the petitioner was not present to speak on the item.

items.title: 2025-61 & 2025-62: Permit Parking Variances at 143 Winthrop Street
items.summary: Denied the permit parking variance requests to park on Martin Street.

items.title: Winthrop Place Safety and Connectivity Recommendation
items.summary: Approved a motion recommending that the mayor and city council allocate resources to improve safety and connectivity on Winthrop Place.

items.title: George Street Handicap Parking Space
items.summary: Approved a motion to establish a handicap parking space on the north side of George Street, replacing an existing 30-minute parking space.

items.title: Martin Street Crosswalk Study
items.summary: Approved a motion directing the engineering division to study the feasibility of installing a crosswalk at Martin Street and Winthrop Street.

items.title: 2025-63: Permit Parking Variance at 612 Main Street
items.summary: Approved a parking variance on Henry Street for a resident of 612 Main Street to mitigate regional parking congestion.

items.title: 2025-64: Porter Road Permit Parking Issues
items.summary: Tabled the request to address permit parking issues because the petitioner was not present.

items.title: 2025-66: Crosswalk Daylighting at Playstead Road and Irving Street
items.summary: Approved a 30-foot parking buffer in front of the commuter rail station crosswalk to improve pedestrian visibility and safety.

items.title: 2025-65: Proposed On-Street EV Charging Stations
items.summary: Discussed a grant-funded proposal to install on-street electric vehicle chargers at five city parks and heard public feedback regarding parking congestion and neighborhood traffic concerns.
